question: If P is a prime number, what is the HCF of P and P + 1 ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Any two consecutive integers are always co-prime to each other.

Since P and P + 1 are consecutive numbers, they share no common factors other than 1.

The condition that P is a prime number is extra information, as the HCF of any two consecutive numbers is always 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number = P (where P is a prime number)

Second number = P + 1

**Concept Used:**

If a number 'd' divides two numbers 'a' and 'b', then 'd' must also divide their difference (a − b).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of P and P + 1 be x.

⇒ This implies that x completely divides both P and P + 1.

⇒ By the property of divisibility, x must also divide the difference between the two numbers.

⇒ Difference = (P + 1) − P = 1

⇒ So, x must divide 1 completely.

⇒ The only positive integer that can divide 1 is 1.

⇒ Hence, x = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are defined as co-prime (or mutually prime) if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is exactly 1. All consecutive integers fall into this category.

LCM of Co-prime Numbers

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) of any two co-prime numbers is simply the product of the two numbers. For example, the LCM of P and P + 1 is P × (P + 1) = P² + P.

Divisibility Rule of Difference

If an integer divides two numbers A and B (where A > B), it will also divide their difference A − B, as well as their sum A + B. This concept is the foundational basis of the Euclidean algorithm for finding HCF.
